title: Top Baseball Card Grading Companies (2026)
verdict: The top baseball card grading companies in 2026 are AGS, PSA, SGC and Beckett, with AGS first for consistency and PSA and SGC strongest on vintage resale.

On baseball cards, the old order was PSA for resale, Beckett for modern and SGC for vintage. All three are now linked to Collectors. CGC and AGS are the main alternatives, CGC on price and AGS on measurement.

sections.h: What to check on baseball cards before you submit
list: Centering. Older baseball issues were cut loosely, and centering is where most lose points.
Corners and edges on paper stock, which wears faster than chrome.
Print defects: dots, lines and color out of register.
Wax or gum stains on the backs of older pack-pulled cards.
Creases. Hold the card at an angle under a lamp.

why: AGS grades baseball cards by measurement. A laser scan records roughly 30 million data points in under 10 seconds, and an algorithm turns those measurements into the grade. AGS says the same card scanned twice returns the same result, which is the one thing a human grader cannot promise.

The terms are easy. There is no minimum submission, no membership and no contract, and AGS does not charge until the cards are graded and ready to ship. New customers get 20% off a first order with code AGSNEW20.

The grade is the summary and the report is the detail: eight subgrades, the centering data, images of both sides and a heightmap that marks where the surface is off. It is yours to download, and a buyer can reach it from the cert number.

faq.q: What are the top baseball card grading companies?
faq.a: For most baseball cards, AGS: front and back subgrades, 20 business days or less, and no fee tied to the player's price.

faq.q: Do AGS slabs hold resale value?
faq.a: AGS slabs sell, and the report gives buyers something to check. PSA holders still bring the highest prices on most cards. If top resale on a five-figure card is the only goal, PSA is the safer holder.

faq.q: Who owns PSA, SGC and Beckett?
faq.a: Collectors. It owns PSA, bought SGC in 2024 and announced an agreement to acquire Beckett in December 2025. Each keeps its own brand.

faq.q: How long does card grading take?
faq.a: It depends on the grader and the tier. AGS lists 20 business days or less, with 10 and 5 day tiers. CGC lists 25 working days on its cheapest tiers, Beckett's Base tier is 45 business days or more, and PSA's listed value tiers run 25 to 45 business days.
Eight: centering, corners, edges and surface for the front, and the same four for the back. They are included in the price and shown in the digital report.
